chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'I intend to perform Tamattu' with the Umrah until the Hajj, so what should I say?' He said, 'You should say,
O Allah, I intend to perform Tamattu' with the Umrah until the Hajj, upon Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
and if you wish, you can keep in mind that which you intend (instead of saying it).

key_terms.أَضْمَرْتَ: You kept silent/intended in the heart
key_terms.تَمَتُّع: Tamattu', a type of Hajj where Umrah and Hajj are performed separately with a break in between
key_terms.حَجّ: Hajj, the major pilgrimage to Mecca
key_terms.عُمْرَة: Umrah, a minor pilgrimage to Mecca
key_terms.كِتَابُكَ: Your Book, referring to the Quran

ai.seo_question: What is the correct formula for the intention (niyyah) of Umrat al-Tamattu according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the flexibility of the niyyah (intention) for Umrat al-Tamattu', emphasizing that the core requirement is the internal resolve to link Umrah with Hajj, which can be expressed verbally or kept silent. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that the verbal declaration serves primarily as a confirmation of the internal intent rather than a rigid ritualistic constraint, grounded in the Quran and Sunnah. This ruling facilitates ease for pilgrims while maintaining the structural integrity of the two Hajj types.
